title: Hypersheaves on the Grothendieck total site as coherent sections
statement:
A small Grothendieck site is a small category with specified covering sieves, containing the maximal sieve and closed under pullback of sieves and transitivity; a sieve is a collection of arrows with fixed target closed under precomposition. A family covers when its generated sieve covers. No fibre products in the underlying category are required. All sizes use [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $\mathbf D(\Lambda)$ be the enhanced localization of cochain complexes of $\Lambda$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms, retaining derived mapping complexes and all higher composition data [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A $\mathbf D(\Lambda)$-valued hypersheaf is a coherent presheaf $F$ such that for every hypercover $T_\bullet\to T$ the map $F(T)\to\operatorname{holim}_{[n]\in\Delta}F(T_n)$ is an equivalence. Here a hypercover is an augmented simplicial family of representable presheaves whose maps to all matching presheaves are locally surjective after sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]; $F$ on a family is the product of its values. Write $\operatorname{Hyp}_{\ge a}(\mathcal C,\Lambda)$ for the full enhanced category of such $F$ with $H^i(F(T))=0$ for every $T$ and $i<a$, for a fixed integer $a$. Morphisms are coherent natural transformations, and mapping complexes are the derived ends in the coherent presheaf category.

Let $I$ be a small poset and $i\mapsto\mathcal C_i$ a strict covariant diagram of small Grothendieck sites. Each transition $\iota_{ij}:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$, $i\le j$, is the inclusion of a full sieve: whenever an object of $\mathcal C_j$ maps to an object of $\mathcal C_i$, its source is also in $\mathcal C_i$. The topology on $\mathcal C_i$ is the restriction of the topology of $\mathcal C_j$; in particular covering sieves of objects of $\mathcal C_i$ are the same in the two sites. Assume the following local lower-refinement condition: whenever $i,j\le k$, $T\in\mathcal C_i$, $S\in\mathcal C_j$ and $S\to T$ is an arrow in $\mathcal C_k$, there is a covering family $\{S_\alpha\to S\}$ in $\mathcal C_j$ and indices $l_\alpha\le i,j$ such that $S_\alpha$ is in the image of $\mathcal C_{l_\alpha}\to\mathcal C_j$. Form the category $\mathcal E$ whose objects are $(i,T)$ with $T\in\mathcal C_i$, and whose morphisms $(i,T)\to(j,S)$ are $i\le j$ and an arrow $\iota_{ij}T\to S$ in $\mathcal C_j$. Give it the topology generated by vertical covering families in each $\mathcal C_i$ and by the singleton families $(i,T)\to(j,\iota_{ij}T)$ with underlying arrow the identity of $T$.

Restriction to the fibres identifies $\operatorname{Hyp}_{\ge a}(\mathcal E,\Lambda)$ with the enhanced homotopy limit
$$\operatorname{holim}_{i\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Hyp}_{\ge a}(\mathcal C_i,\Lambda).$$
Thus the objects on the right are coherent systems $F_i$ with equivalences $\iota_{ij}^*F_j\simeq F_i$ and all composition homotopies. On presheaves before imposing descent, restriction identifies coherent presheaves on $\mathcal E$ with coherent sections of the fibre presheaf diagram; inversion of the indicated identity-underlying arrows imposes precisely these equivalences. Under this comparison the hypersheaf condition is exactly hyperdescent on every fibre together with inversion of these arrows. Derived mapping complexes on both sides are the same homotopy coherent ends over strings of arrows of $\mathcal E$, and the comparison respects composition. The equivalence is natural for inclusions of indexing posets and compatible diagrams of these sieve inclusions, and it preserves the pointwise lower bound $a$.
